newsitem.title: USA: D.A. to drop charges against Orange County official.
newsitem.headline: D.A. to drop charges against Orange County official.

text.p: The district attorney of Orange County, Calif., has agreed to drop felony charges against the county's former budget director Monday in exchange for his no-contest plea to a misdemeanor, people involved in the proposed plea bargain said Friday.
Under the agreement, former Budget Director Ronald Rubino, 44, will plead no contest to a record-keeping violation to avoid a new trial stemming from Orange County's historic bankruptcy.

Under the terms of the deal, Rubino will be given 100 hours of community service and two years of unsupervised probation, they said. The felony charges carried a maximum punishment of nine years in prison.

In a letter to the southern California county's Board of Supervisors, Rubino continued to assert his innocence of any charges. He said it was in the best interest of his family, friends and the public to put an end to "this ordeal."

In a no-contest plea, a defendant does not admit guilt but states he or she will offer no defense. The person is then subject to being judged guilty and punished as if he or she had pleaded guilty or had been convicted.

Under the deal, Rubino will petition the court at the end of the first year of his probation to withdraw his no-contest plea and enter a plea of innocent. The misdemeanor charge will then be dismissed.

Rubino was indicted by a county grand jury in December 1995 on two felony charges accusing him of helping former county Treasurer Robert Citron divert funds from other government agencies for the county's benefit.
His trial, the first criminal trial arising from the Orange County bankruptcy, began in August but ended in a mistrial Sept. 13. A new trial was set to begin next week.

After the mistrial was declared, Orange County District Attorney Michael Capizzi said his office would immediately retry Rubino. But some county supervisors and members of the public have since called on Capizzi to drop the case.

By pleading no contest to the single misdemeanor, Rubino will avoid the retrial, people involved in the negotiations said. An attorney for Rubino declined to comment on the deal pending a hearing Monday in Santa Ana, the Orange County seat.
Officials in the county district attorney's office were not immediately available to comment.
Orange County filed for bankruptcy protection on Dec. 6, 1994, after sustaining investment losses of more than $1.6 billion. The county emerged from bankruptcy last June.
Citron, who pleaded guilty in April 1995 to six felony charges stemming from the bankruptcy, is awaiting sentencing. Other former and current county officials have yet to be tried.
